newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says summit to proceed despite injury.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says summit to proceed despite injury.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Friday that a summit with Russian President Boris Yeltsin would proceed in Helsinki next week despite a knee injury for which Clinton will have surgery.

"It will go on, you bet," Clinton told reporters as he was lifted in a wheelchair onto Air Force One for a flight back to Washington for knee surgery. He was taken to hospital in Florida after a fall at the estate of golfer Greg Norman.
Clinton, who fell on some steps in the early hours of Friday morning and tore a tendon in his right knee, is due to have surgery at Bethesda Naval Hospital outside Washington later on Friday.
Doctors said he would make a full recovery but faced weeks of rehabilitation.

The president managed a smile and a thumbs-up when asked by reporters how he felt as aides lifted him backwards up the steps of the airplane in a wheelchair, his right leg immobilized and sticking straight out. "I feel good," he said.

He is due to arrive in Helsinki on Wednesday for two days of talks with Yeltsin. The dates of the summit had earlier been in doubt because of the health of Yeltsin, who is recovering from heart surgery and pneumonia.
